table.title: Strikes in January, 1928
table.caption_extra: The following is a summary of the strikes during January 1928.* Note:—To economize space full details are only given of strikes affecting 500 or more workers and lasting more than one day.

rows: Redwood and Hardwood Furnitures Makers Labour Union, 92 Nan Chieh, Wai Ma Lu Chiao, Great South Gate, Shanghai:
China Electric Co., Ltd., 628 Chang An Road, Chapei, Shanghai:
Wheelbarrow Coolies Working for various Rice Hongs along the Soochow Creek in Chapei, Shanghai.
Dry Goods Employees' Union, 512 Hsi Lin Road, Outside West Gate, Shanghai:
Failure on part of the employers to grant (or revise) the five demands submitted by their employees over a month before.
(1) That the conditions embodied in their old agreement be put in force. (2) That the practice of employing temporary workers be abolished. (3) That positions be secured for dismissed workers.

Through the mediation of Chinese authorities and with mutual consent of the employers and the employees, the following revised agreement was drafted and signed on January 13, 1928: (1) That the employees' union shall be recognized as the sole representative of the employees. (2) That medical expenses in cases of sickness shall be borne by the employers and that due compensation be paid to the family of the deceased in case of death resulting from injuries received while on duty. (3) That the maximum number of working hours per day shall not exceed 14 with the exception of the 12th moon of the lunar year. (4) That if a shop is insured, the insurance shall cover the belongings of the employees at the estimated worth of Tls. 40 each. (5) That the wages of those receiving less than $6 per month shall be increased to $9, which amount shall be regarded as the minimum wage per month, and that those receiving more than $6 per month shall receive a general increase of $3 each. (6) That the monthly fee to apprentices shall be increased from [illegible] to $1.00. (7) That the annual subsidy to apprentices shall be increased from $2 to $10 each for those in the 1st year of apprenticeship, from $4 to [illegible] for those in the 2nd year, and from $8 to [illegible] for those in the 3rd year; and that the wages for those who have finished the term of apprenticeship shall be $5 per month each for the 1st year, $7 for the 2nd year, and $9 for the 3rd year. (8) That discarded wrappers, sacks, wooden cases, strings and ropes, etc., be given to employees as perquisites. (9) Double wages (one month) at the end of every year. (10) That the 3rd and 9th moons of a year shall be the periods during which the employers may discharge or engage workers, and in case of dismissal, the dismissed shall receive $8 extra. (11) That non-members of the employees' union shall not be engaged. (12) That the practice of employing workers for a temporary time only shall be abolished. (13) That shops employing more than 6 workers shall take in and give work to 1 unemployed member of the union, and those employing more than 10 workers shall take in 2.
Piece Goods Employees' Union, No. 7 Branch Union, 1 Chi Shan Li, E. Seward Road, Shanghai:
Book-binders' Labour Union, 147 Te Yung Li, Paochang Road, Chapei, Shanghai.
Rice Shop Employees' Union.* Nantao Address: Yin Fu Li, Hou Chia Road, Nantao, Shanghai. Chapei Address: 24 San I Li, Yung Hsing Road, Chapei, Shanghai.

200 employed by 300 shops in Nantao and 400 employed by 300 shops in Chapei. (These numbers of "workers on Strike" represent 50 per cent. of the total numbers of workers in employment, which are respectively 400 and 800).
Failure on part of the employers to carry out last year's agreement which ensures higher wages and better working conditions.

That the agreement be put in force:— (1) Recognition of the workers' union as their sole representative. (2) A rent subsidy of $20 per month to the union for period of one yaar. (3) The minimum monthly salaries for employees to be as follows: $20 (formerly $14-$15) each for managers, $17 (formerly around $10) each for accountants and other chief employees, $14 (formerly $7-$8) each for ordinary employees, and $7 (formerly $2-$4) each for workers who have finished apprenticeship. (4) 5 days' extra pay per month for any worker who has never missed a day's work during the whole month, and double wages (one month) at the end of every lunar year for all workers. (5) Increase of wages once every year. (6) A fee of 2 cents per picul (formerly half a cent) for workers who sift rice and that of $4 for every 1,000 piculs of rice piled up. (7) 10 dimes instead of 5 dimes to be given to each of the apprentices as his monthly fee. (8) Annual subsidies to apprentices to be increased from $4 to $12 for the 1st year, from $8 to $24 for the 2nd year, and from $12 to $36 for the 3rd year. (9) Open accounts. (10) Three-tenths of the annual profits to be distributed among the employees as bonus. (11) Employees and apprentices free to become members of their labour union. (12) That non-union members be not selected for employment. (13) No dismissal of workers without reason. (14) Employers' household servants shall pay for their food. (15) Reduction of working hours per day from 16 to 12. (16) Free medical treatment to sick workers. (17) Due compensation to the family of any worker who dies from injuries received while on duty. (18) No heavy work for apprentices.
Shanghai Pawnshop Employees represented by the Nantao Pawnshop Workers' Union. 7 Wu Chia Lung, Old North Gate, Shanghai:
No increase in wages as promised and the dismissal of several workers in different shops.

(1) Recognition of the representative right of the workers' union. (2) A general increase of wages. (3) 3 years' apprenticeship with a subsidy of $1 per month for apprentices in the 1st year, $2 for those in the 2nd year, and $3 for those in tha 3rd year. (4) Distribution of 25 per cent. of the total net profits among workers as bonus. (5) Substitution of pawnshop union members for workers who have resigned or been dismissed. (6) No dismissal without reason, and in case of dismissal with good reason a retiring fee equivalent to 8 months' wages to be paid to the dismissed. (7) In case of bankruptcy or assets being sold to another management, extra pay to be given to workers. (8) An account statement to be rendered annually. (9) Reduction of working hours to 9 per day. (10) 2 months' leave every year with full pay. (11) 2 weeks' leave on occasion of a wedding or funeral in worker's family. (12) Compensation to the family of any worker killed by accident while on duty or while doing service for the shop.

The above demands were granted in an agreement duly signed on December 31 at the Bureau of Agriculture, Industry, and Commerce in the presence of representatives from the workers' union, the pawnshop owners' associations, the Unification Committee of Shanghai Labour Unions, and the Bureau, effective on January 6, 1928.
Cantonese Grocery Employees' Union, Te Lin Fang, Jukong Road, Chapei, Shanghai:
Failure on part of employers to grant employees' demands for wage increases and better working conditions.

(1) Recognition of the employees' union. (2) Non-union members not to be employed. (3) No dismissal of workers without reason. (4) Working hours from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. every day and extra pay for extra work on the basis of a full day's wage. (5) Double wages (one month) at the end of every lunar year. (6) Fowl feathers, pork bones, wooden cases, and wrappers, etc., to be given to employees as perquisites. (7) Only one apprentice to be taken in by a shop employing over 10 workers and two apprentices by that employing over 20 workers, and the period of apprenticeship to cover 3 years only. (8) Distribution of 20 per cent. of the annual net profits among workers as bonus. (9) A general increase of $2 each per month, besides $6 each for those receiving less than $5, $5 for those receiving less than $15, and $3 for those receiving less than $20.

(1) The employee's union shall be recognized. (2) That when engaging new workers, the employment of union members shall be first considered. (3) That no workers shall be dismissed without reason. (4) That employees shall work every day from 7 a.m. to 9.30 p.m. (5) That leave must be obtained if a worker desires to go out during working hours; otherwise, due reduction in his wages shall be made. (6) Double wages (one month) at the end of a year. (7) That apprentices after the period of three years shall receive $2 per month. (8) That the 10th of October and other national and festival days shall be observed as holidays with full pay. (9) That fowl feathers, pork bones, and discarded wooden cases and wrappers shall be given to employees as a perquisite. (10) That wage increases shall be made every year as the employers see fit, the minimum to be $1 each.
Sauce Shop Employees' Union, 48 Fu Yu Road, Native City, Shanghai:
Failure on part of the managements of 300 ordinary sauce shops to abide by the agreement signed on May 26, 1927, between the employers and the employees.

That the said agreement be carried into execution immediately, which embodies the following:— (1) That the employees' union shall be recognized. (2) That the employees have a right to become members of the union. (3) That all wages shall be increased according to the schedule agreed upon. (4) That apprentices shall be admitted only once in every three years. (5) That each employee shall be entitled to 36 hours' leave per month at ordinary times. (6) That the shop owners and managers shall not employ their own relatives or those who are not in the sauce business. (7) That 30 per cent. of the total annual net profits shall be distributed among the employees as bonus. (8) That accounts shall be rendered at the end of every year. (9) That the working hours per day shall not exceed 12. (10) That no workers shall be dismissed without reason. (11) That apprentices shall not be maltreated. (12) That in case of sickness, the medical expenses of the workers shall be borne by the management, and in case of death resulting from injuries received while on duty, due compensation shall be paid.

(1) That the above conditions shall be fulfilled. (2) That full pay shall be issued to workers during the period of strike. (3) That no workers shall be dismissed on account of the strike. (4) That the employees' union shall receive from the employers a monthly subsidy of $20.

Terms of settlement are embodied in an agreement signed between representatives of the company and of the strikers at the residence of Mr. T. V. Soong, Nationalist Minister of Finance, on January 16, 1928, in presence of the Chief of the Labour and Peasant Division of the Shanghai Party Bureau, a representative of the Labour and Merchants Division of the Shanghai Municipality, and the Chief of the Kiangsu Cigarette Bureau of the Ministry of Finance. The English text reads as follows:— (1) The B. A. T. factory authorities, hereinafter called the "Factory authorities," recognize that the Workers of the B. A. T. factories, hereinafter called the "Workers" have the right to organize within the scope of the law a labour union. The said labour union shall be an organization to represent the workers for the promotion of their benefit. (2) The factory authorities shall not dismiss any workers without cause. Dismissals shall be made in accordance with the factory regulations. (3) For the benefit of the workers, the factory authorities have established a school and an appropriate name shall be given to this school. The running expenses thereof shall be borne by the factory authorities. The name of the said school shall be "School for B. A. T. Women's Children." (4) According to the existing arrangements, the rice allowance is based on $8. The factory authorities now agree to set it at $5. Rice allowance will be given to all workers without discrimination unless they are absent without leave granted by the factory authorities. (5) The factory authorities agree to give a total of six weeks' leave of absence, without pay, to woman workers on account of child birth, and a payment of $30 to each woman worker will be paid on such occasions. (6) In case a worker is unable to work on account of illness the factory authorities shall designate a hospital, pay the usual wages, and also pay the required hospital expenses. In case of death through illness the factory authorities shall duly consider a grant to the family of the deceased. (7) In case a worker dies as a result of an accident whilst discharging his or her duty the factory authorities shall pay once and for all a total compensation amounting to $1,500. (8) The bonus to be given at the end of this lunar year shall be paid on the basis of 12 months' work, that is to say, no deduction will be made for the period of strike. (9) All points that have not been touched upon by the foregoing terms shall be dealt with according to existing regulations and customs in the factories. (10) The agreement after its execution shall be adhered to by both parties until promulgation of the labour laws by the Nationalist Government (11) The agreement shall take effect from the date of its execution.

table.title: Strikes in February, 1928
table.caption_extra: The following is a summary of the strikes during February:*

rows: Wheel-barrow Coolies Working for Rice Hongs in Chapei, Shanghai: (Cf. Summary of Strikes for January.)
The coolies resumed work when the Chairman of the Chapei Rice Merchants' Guild promised to negotiate with the Public Utility Bureau on their behalf.
Bookbinders' Labour Union, 147 Te Yung Li, Paochang Road, Chapei, Shanghai: (Cf. Summary of strikes for January.)
Refusal of employers to accept the workers' demands sent in during the strike from January 15 to 19.
That the demands sent in be granted and put in force.

The workers returned to work on February 18 pending the drafting of a new agreement with the employers, which was duly signed by both parties on February 24 in presence of representatives from the Labour Union Unification Committee and the Bureau of Agriculture, Labour, and Commerce. The conditions are as follows:— (1) That the Binders' Labour Union shall be recognized as the representative organ of the workers. (2) That no workers shall be dismissed without cause and, in case of a dismissal, a subsidy equivalent to one or two months' wages shall be given to the worker dismissed, besides one month's notice. (3) That none of the workers who are members of the executive committee of the labour union shall be discharged for any reason other than the violation of the rules of the works. (4) That the working hours shall be reduced to 9½ a day and that every 5 hours of night work or 8 hours' work on Sundays shall be counted as full day's work entitled to a full day's pay and every 3 hours' night work as half a day's work with half a day's full pay. (5) That every Sunday, October 10, Mid-Autumn Festival Day, Dragon Boat Festival Day, January 1, and other special commemoration days shall be observed as holidays with full pay, besides 6 days holiday for China New Year. If any of the above days happens to fall on Sunday, a week-day shall be given as holiday in its place. In case any of the workers are willing to work on holidays, double pay shall be given to regular workers and an extra pay of $0.10-25 each for piece workers. (6) That a monthly subsidy of $1.00 shall be given to each apprentice in his first year, $2.00 in the second year, and $3.00 in the third year, and that after three years' apprenticeship each apprentice shall receive $8.00 per month as wages. Apprentices who have worked more than 15 nights in a month are entitled to a special subsidy of $1.00 each that month. Employees who work during the night shall receive a special rice allowance. (7) That 1 to 2 weeks' leave shall be granted to a worker who has a wedding or funeral in his family, and 1 month's leave to a woman worker on account of child birth, with the understanding that due reduction in wages shall be made if workers do not report when their leave expires, and that workers shall be dismissed if absent for 2 or more weeks without permission. (8) That extra pay of half a month's wages shall be granted every year to every worker who has not been absent from work more than 10 days during the whole year. (9) That an increase in wages shall be granted once a year on the following basis: $2.00 increase per month for each man worker, $1.50 for each woman, and $1.25 for each piece worker. (10) That the system of engaging small contractors shall be abolished. (11) That full pay shall be issued to workers on sick leave, up to 2 months. (12) That employees shall have free choice whether or not to take board and lodging in the works. (13) That fractions of a dollar of wages shall be paid according to the big money scale. (14) That a food allowance of $7.00 per month shall be paid to any worker who eats his own food. (15) That only 2 apprentices shall be admitted every 3 years. (16) That this agreement shall take effect from the date of its execution and shall be adhered to by both parties for a year.
Toa Seima Kaisha, Robinson Road, Shanghai:
Dismissal of 2 workers because of their negligence in work.
The workers returned to work when the management consented to give a retirement subsidy to the dismissed.

(1) That the manager of the Wei Lung filature, the police sergeant in charge, and a policeman, alleged to have been the chief assailant, be arrested and severely punished. 1 day and 6 hours (2 hours in the afternoon of May 24, 4 hours in the afternoon of May 25, and whole day of May 26).
200 girl workers in the packing room, affecting the whole body of workers in the factory numbering 700, 400 girls and women and 300 men.
Failure on part of the management to grant the workers' demand for wage increases.

(1) That wages be increased. (2) That no fines be imposed if any boxes among the packed ones be found to be empty. (3) That the factory premises be cleaned by coolies employed specially for that purpose and not by the workers themselves. (4) That the matches be kept dry when ready to be packed so that the packers may not waste time in drying the matches.

Hsiang Chang Silk and Cotton Weaving Factory, 36 Rue Amiral Bayle, Shanghai:
Second-hand Clothing Shop Employees' Union, 6 Tien Teng Chieh, Native City, Shanghai.

Quarrel and subsequent fighting between two union members and the Tai H'u shop people who are said to have opened their shop before the scheduled time in disobedience of union rules, which fighting resulted in the two inspectors being arrested by the police and put in jail.

(1) Release of the two inspectors; compensation for all losses sustained by the two inspectors, non-dismissal within a year; and $20 a day compensation for each of the two inspectors during their stay in jail. (2) $1 a day compensation for every worker during the period of strike. (3) Dismissal of non-union-member workers. (4) Adherence to the time schedule decided upon by the union. (5) No dismissal of workers on account of the strike. (6) Dismissal of Weng Jui-sheng who is alleged to have started the fight. (7) Guarantee that no similar occurrence should happen in the future.

rows: Hsiang Chang Silk and Cotton Weaving Factory, 36 Rue Amiral Bayle, Shanghai: (Cf. Summary of Strikes for May, 1928.)
Second-hand Clothing Shop Employees' Union, 6 Tien Teng Chieh, Native City, Shanghai: (Cf. Summary of Strikes for May, 1928.)

(1) A compensation fund of $120 for each of the two inspectors in jail and guarantee of their non-dismissal within a year by their employers after expiration of the sentence. (2) Dismissal of Weng Jui-seng (翁瑞生), the alleged starter of the fight, from service in Tai H'u shop and nullification of his membership to the employees' union, effective till January 1, 1929. (3) No dismissal of workers on account of the strike. (4) $4 special grant to each worker during the period of strike. (5) All employees, with the exception of managers and those holding important offices, to be members of the workers' union. June 25, 1928, when all the workers returned to work with the exception of those of the 21 filatures in Hutung (East Shanghai), 3 in Chapei, and 2 in Nantao. July 5, 1928, when the above filature workers also resumed work, thus terminating the strike.
5,000 men, 50,000 women, and 10,000 juveniles, totalling 65,000 workers.

Originally, disatisfaction with the judgment of the Chinese Court in connection with the death of an employee of the Wei Lun Silk Filature, who is alleged to have died from wounds inflicted by a Chapei police constable during a fracas in the factory. (Cf. Summary of Strikes for March, 1928.) (The judgment sentenced the police constable to eight years' imprisonment, but exonerated the owner of the filature and a Chinese police sergeant who, the workers alleged, were responsible for the conflict, and also passed sentence of eighteen months in gaol on two workers for conduct detrimental to public peace.)

(1) Release of two workers under sentence. (2) Payment of $8,630 to the family of the deceased worker by the owner of the Wei Lun Filature. (3) Punishment of the police sergeant. (4) Payment of $3,000 to the labour union as reimbursement of expenses incurred by them in fighting the case. (5) Payment of wages to workers of the Wei Lun Filature for March, April, and May. (6) No dismissal of workers in Wei Lun on account of the strike. (7) Approval of the labour union necessary in cases of dismissal. Sub-demands presented by Women Workers: (1) Full pay during the period of strike. (2) Increase of wages. (3) Reduction of working hours from 11 hours and 1 quarter per day to 10. (4) Fraction of a dollar to be calculated in big money.

(1) $3,000 compensation to the family of the deceased worker, which sum will be deposited in a bank to the credit of the relatives who will receive the monthly interest and the whole sum after 30 years. (2) $900 to the family to cover funeral expenses. (3) $1,700 to the union to compensate losses. (4) A bonus equivalent to 4 days' wages to workers to cover the period of strike. (5) A flat increase of 2 cents big money per day in wages of women workers. (6) Increase by 10 cents big money from $0.20 to $0.30 in the weekly bonus for meritorious work to women workers.
